notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware, Docker, Gazebo or PX4 run was made. The gate cannot import the upstream aas-gym (it needs Python ^3.12, numpy, gymnasium, docker and pyzmq; aas-gym/pyproject.toml:11-18) and package code never imports or runs the clone, so the fake backend is this package's pure Python clock recording fake (fake.py). It models only the /clock observation, the constant -1 step reward, the step_count truncation and the reset's 80 s init run; it does not model Gazebo/PX4 dynamics, contacts, actuators, sensors, wind, camera or LiDAR, and its start clock and increments are placeholder test data. The sim backend (gymnasium.make('AASEnv-v0')) was not run: registration is in tools_and_docs/gym_run.py:17-20 and the full Docker/Gazebo stack is required. The declared fidelity is the checked model (engine analytic, level F0, determinism none, nominal 20 ms control period, lockstep clock), not a claim about the unrun Gazebo/PX4 simulation, and its gaps say so. NOT COVERED: the Gazebo/PX4 simulation itself, rendering, the camera and LiDAR streams, and the physical effect of the action. The observation array is the same two-element /clock as upstream, so no array is reduced. Five warnings are expected of a Gymnasium family driver (PLAYBOOK.md section 8): G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (it only sets the seed of the next reset) and four G8.NO_UNIT for the bridge-derived inputs (seed twice, ticks, action.values). G4 had no REF_VALUE or REF_BINARY warnings. Only catalogue classes are used (cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1, cap.world.seed.v1), so there are no catalogue requests. gate.digest is the digest the check printed (the check report without its clock); check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
